observations.detail: Full-disk SDO/AIA 193 Å image at 2026-10-24 15:17:05 UT shows coronal loop structures, bright active regions, and darker coronal-hole-like regions.
A single static AIA image cannot confirm an Earth-directed CME; coronagraph or running-difference imagery is required.
NOAA forecast: max Kp = 3.33 until 2026-10-25 00:34 UTC.
NOAA alert ALTK04: K-index of 4 reached 2026 Oct 23 1953 UTC; impacts primarily poleward of 65° geomagnetic latitude.
NOAA alert ALTEF3: 2 MeV integral flux exceeded 1,000 pfu; maximum 3,169 pfu on 2026 Oct 23 1540 UTC.

assessment.risk_reasoning: Recent geomagnetic activity (Kp 4.33) and elevated >2 MeV electron flux indicate enhanced thermospheric density and increased drag on LEO satellites. However, the forecast Kp is declining to 3.33, no geomagnetic storm scales are active, and no Earth-directed CME is confirmed from the single image, so severe drag escalation is not expected. Uncertainty remains elevated for high-area-to-mass objects.
assessment.orbit_prediction_impact: Orbit prediction reliability is moderately reduced over the next 72 hours due to elevated and variable atmospheric drag. More frequent orbit determination and collision avoidance reassessment are advisable, particularly for low-altitude or high-area-to-mass-ratio LEO assets, though maneuver planning should not assume storm-level density enhancements.

trace.policy_text: Manoeuvre when Pc >= 1e-4 and a verified option exists. Between 1e-5 and 1e-4, or when Pc is diluted, prefer getting precise data if there is time before the latest safe burn. Never manoeuvre if our propulsion status is unverified. If the other object is an active satellite that can manoeuvre, contact its operator before moving; if it is an operational satellite whose capability is unknown, notify its operator. Keep at least 30 minutes for command upload. Max 1.0 m/s per burn.

decision.rationale: Pc exceeds maneuver threshold (4.4e-4) but the risk is diluted, indicating possible higher Pc with better data. There is ample time (>8 h) before the latest safe burn (O2) and sufficient lead for command upload (>30 min). Policy therefore prefers obtaining precise ephemeris/CDM before committing to a burn, while also notifying the other operator whose maneuver capability is unknown.
